Lessons.Title: Calculating Measures of Center and Variability
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: calculate and interpret mean, median, mean absolute deviation (MAD) and interquartile range (IQR), naming their units and the quartile convention. Original Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 1 Lesson 5, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/1/5/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0). This is optional review; publisher Building On 6.SP.B.5.c and Building Towards HSS-ID.A.1, HSS-ID.A.2, not a publisher Addressing lesson.

Original hypothetical data: walk durations 4,6,6,8,11 minutes. Mean=(4+6+6+8+11)/5=7; median=6. Under median-of-halves with central value excluded, Q1=(4+6)/2=5 and Q3=(8+11)/2=9.5; IQR=4.5 minutes. Absolute deviations from mean 7 are 3,1,1,1,4, so MAD=10/5=2 minutes. The longer walk increases the mean more than the median.

Class activity: organize every absolute deviation in a table, draw a number line locating mean/median/quartiles, then discuss what center and variability mean for the hypothetical sample. Compare two other sets with equal means and different MADs. If actual class measurements are collected, use authorized anonymous observations, never fabricate participation.

Teacher-scored rubric: 0–2 each for sorted data and stated quartile rule, correct mean/median, all absolute deviations and MAD, and comparison with appropriate units (8 maximum). Teacher judgement is required for explanation and interpretation; a numeric answer cannot stand in for a physical meter-stick investigation.

V12 optional-source-status correction: IM Algebra 1 Unit 1 Lesson 5 is an OPTIONAL BELOW-GRADE-LEVEL review. Before assigning it, an authorized teacher examines the pre-unit diagnostic: if students can already calculate mean, median, mean absolute deviation and IQR accurately, the lesson may be skipped. A skipped optional lesson is not a failed required academic standard, nor proof that an assessment was administered. Official teacher/student sources: https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/1/5/preparation.html and https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/1/5/index.html.

V12 original additional task: seven fictional measurements in minutes [3,5,5,7,9,9,11]. Their mean is7, median7, lower quartile5 and upper quartile9 under median-of-halves convention, IQR4 minutes, absolute deviations [4,2,2,0,2,2,4] and MAD16/7≈2.286 minutes. Plot dots and a correctly scaled number line. In pairs, explain why a median and MAD answer different questions. The official student activities include a physical meter-stick demonstration and heartbeat tables, but a text-only draft does not constitute an actually conducted demonstration.

V12 proposed teacher rubric (0–2 each, total8): original seven-point data plot and quartiles; correct mean, median, IQR and MAD with units; explanation and chosen quartile convention; genuine activity/diagnostic evidence if performed. Optional status must be respected in reporting.

KeyConcepts.Title: Mean and median
KeyConcepts.Definition: Mean is sum divided by count; median is the middle ordered value.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Sort for median and use units throughout.

KeyConcepts.Title: Mean absolute deviation
KeyConcepts.Definition: MAD is the average absolute distance from the mean.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Compute the mean before absolute deviations.

KeyConcepts.Title: Interquartile range
KeyConcepts.Example: Q1=5 and Q3=9.5 give IQR 4.5 minutes.

WorkedExamples.Title: Calculate center and quartiles
WorkedExamples.Question: Find the statistics for sorted walk durations 4,6,6,8,11.
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain each calculation and verify it independently.
Steps: Sum 4+6+6+8+11=35; divide by 5 to obtain mean 7.
The third of five observations is 6, so the median is 6.
Exclude the central 6; lower pair 4,6 has Q1=5.
Upper pair 8,11 has Q3=9.5; subtract for IQR=4.5.

WorkedExamples.Title: Calculate MAD
WorkedExamples.Question: Using the same five walk durations, compute average absolute deviation from mean.
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain each calculation and verify it independently.
Steps: Divide by five values: MAD=2 minutes.
WorkedExamples.Check: Absolute distances are nonnegative and have time units.

WorkedExamples.Title: Same center, different spread
WorkedExamples.Question: Compare A=3,5,7 and B=1,5,9.
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain each calculation and verify it independently.
Steps: Both sums equal 15 and each sample has three observations; means equal 5.
Both ordered middle values equal 5; medians equal 5.
For A absolute deviations are 2,0,2, so MAD=4/3.
For B deviations are 4,0,4, so MAD=8/3.
The second sample is more variable despite identical center.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Means 5 and medians 5; B has twice the MAD.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Signed deviations about a mean add to zero.
The defined mean absolute deviation here is about the mean.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming all software uses identical quartiles
CommonMistakes.Correction: Declare median-of-halves and use it consistently.

SummaryPoints: Mean and median summarize location; MAD and IQR quantify variability.
For 4,6,6,8,11: mean 7, median 6, MAD 2, IQR 4.5 minutes.
Outliers can affect mean more strongly than median.
Teacher-reviewed interpretation must not be replaced with a generic numeric quiz.
